title: Samsung Unveils Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 With Major Battery Upgrades
excerpt: The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 packs an 800mAh battery — a 35% jump over its predecessor — alongside a new Snapdragon Wear Elite chip and 5,000-nit display brightness.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Samsung launched Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 with an 800mAh battery, a 35% increase from its predecessor.
  • Both new watches switch to Qualcomm's Snapdragon Wear Elite chip for better performance and efficiency.
  • New health features include sleep apnea detection, heart health score, and hydration tracking.
  • Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 starts at £649, while Watch 9 begins at £349, with preorders open now.

Samsung's Wearable Bet Gets Bigger

Samsung used its Galaxy Unpacked event in London on July 22 to launch two new smartwatches that prioritize battery life and raw performance. The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, aimed at athletes and outdoor enthusiasts, features an 800mAh battery — up from 590mAh in the original Ultra — representing a 35% increase in capacity. The standard Galaxy Watch 9 also gets a battery bump in its larger 44mm variant, rising to 445mAh from its predecessor's capacity.

The battery improvements are paired with a significant processor change. Both watches move from Samsung's in-house Exynos W1000 chip to Qualcomm's Snapdragon Wear Elite SW6100 platform. Samsung says the new chip delivers faster performance and better power efficiency, which combined with the larger batteries should translate into meaningfully longer usage between charges.

Ultra 2: Built for Extremes

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is Samsung's answer to Apple's Ultra line, and the spec sheet makes the ambition clear. The 47mm titanium-framed watch features a display capable of 5,000 nits of peak brightness — making it readable in direct sunlight — and carries an IP69K dust and water resistance rating. It is water-resistant to 100 meters and is 12% thinner than the original Ultra at approximately 10.6mm.

Samsung introduced several features targeting specific activities. Trail Run tracks elevation gain, climbing progress, and terrain impact, with the company claiming it helps reduce injury risk. A new Sweat Loss feature estimates water loss during exercise and recommends rehydration timing. Later this year, Samsung plans to launch an Ultra 2 Diving app with advanced features including ascent and descent speed tracking and safe dive limits.

The watch also supports turn-by-turn navigation for GPX routes — a direct appeal to hikers and trail runners who rely on pre-planned paths in areas without cellular coverage.

Watch 9: Incremental but Meaningful

The Galaxy Watch 9 receives more modest upgrades. The 40mm model retains a 325mAh battery, while the 44mm version bumps up to 445mAh. Both models use aluminum cases and carry a 5 ATM water resistance rating. The display resolutions are 438 x 438 pixels for the 40mm and 480 x 480 for the 44mm variant.

Samsung added a Vitals feature that monitors key health metrics overnight, including respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood oxygen levels. Both the Watch 9 and Ultra 2 share enhanced health-tracking capabilities: improved sleep apnea detection cleared by the FDA, and a heart health score that aggregates cardiovascular data into a single, trackable metric.

All models ship with Bluetooth 6.0, NFC, dual-band Wi-Fi, and Wear OS 7 running Samsung's One UI 9 Watch interface. LTE variants are available across the lineup.

Pricing and Availability

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is priced at £649 (approximately €749) and comes in Titanium Silver and Titanium Grey. The Galaxy Watch 9 starts at £349 for the 40mm Bluetooth model in Cream or Graphite, and £379 for the 44mm version in Silver or Graphite. LTE variants add roughly £50 to each price point.

Preorders opened immediately following the announcement, with Samsung confirming shipments will begin August 7.

The Qualcomm Factor

The shift to Qualcomm silicon across Samsung's entire wearable lineup is a notable strategic move. Industry analyst Paolo Pescatore of PP Foresight called it "a significant endorsement" of Qualcomm's strategy to extend its silicon across personal devices, noting that Qualcomm now powers Samsung's smartphones, foldables, watches, and upcoming smart eyewear.

For consumers, the practical implication is third-party app performance. Qualcomm's Snapdragon Wear platform has broader developer support than Samsung's Exynos wearable chips, which could translate into smoother experiences for apps ranging from Google Maps to Spotify.

What It Means for Indian Buyers

Samsung typically launches Galaxy Watch products in India within weeks of the global debut. Indian pricing for the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is expected to land around ₹62,000-65,000, while the Watch 9 could start near ₹34,000. The health-tracking features — particularly sleep apnea detection and the heart health score — align with growing wellness awareness among Indian consumers, though the Ultra 2's premium pricing will limit its audience to fitness enthusiasts and early adopters.
